target_customer: Finance teams at companies that make, move, build or operate things, such as manufacturers and logistics firms
problem: Operating records (production runs, shipments, work orders) and the ledger describe the same business in different shapes, so linking operating changes to financial results lives in spreadsheets.
business_model: B2B software connecting read-only to operational and financial systems; pricing not found
product_category: AI ontology layer linking operational data to finance

founders.name: Gurshabd Singh Varaich
founders.background_notes: YC page: wallet policy and approval controls at BitGo.

competitors.name: Rillet
competitors.what: AI-native ERP for finance teams, partners with an operations platform for inventory and production

competitors.name: Campfire
competitors.what: AI-native ERP and accounting; a guide says it cannot run production or inventory operations

technical_complexity.rationale: Mapping operational records to ledger structures across many ERP and production systems is integration-heavy, with deterministic rules for traceability.

defensibility.rationale: Deep read-only integrations and a mapped ontology can lock in finance workflows, but the company is brand new and adjacent ERP vendors could expand.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of 2026 sources, AI-native ERPs do not handle production costing directly; no move against Definite found.

market_need_then: Founders describe controllers rebuilding the same spreadsheet monthly to tie production systems to the ledger; a 2026 guide identifies job costing and WIP valuation as poorly handled by general AI finance tools.

branding.domain_note: Uses usedefinite.com, so the plain definite.com domain was not used.

identity.voice_and_tone: Precise and trust-focused, describing itself as the ontology layer for finance.

branding.community_and_virality: No brand press found; a different company called Definite (AI data platform, $10M seed in 2025) shares the name.

brand_strength.rationale: A same-named data analytics company already raised publicly in 2025, which makes searches ambiguous, and no brand press exists.

outcome_analysis: Definite is an active Fall 2026 company of three Waterloo engineers with fintech and trading backgrounds, so no outcome has occurred. The founders' narrative of watching a controller rebuild a spreadsheet is a real pain, but the name collides with an unrelated funded company and the niche is adjacent to fast-moving AI ERPs.
